:::{#def-channel-capacity}
#### Channel capacity

Send one [input](#def-channel) $X$ through a [discrete memoryless channel](#def-channel),
and let $Y$ be the output.
The [joint distribution](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/random-variables.html#def-joint-distribution) of $(X, Y)$ is
$\P(X = x, Y = y) = \P(X = x) \, p(y \mid x)$,
so the
[mutual information](entropy.qmd#def-mutual-information) $\mutinfof{X}{Y}$
depends on the channel and on the input [probability mass function](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/random-variables.html#def-pmf).
The **capacity** of the channel is the largest mutual information
any choice of $X$ achieves:

$$C \eqdef \max_{\P(X = \cdot)} \mutinfof{X}{Y},$$

where the [maximum](https://morrison-lab.github.io/mds/algebra-basics.html#def-maximum) runs over all [probability mass functions](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/random-variables.html#def-pmf) on $\mathcal{X}$
[@cover2006elements, chapter 7].
With base-2 [logarithms](https://morrison-lab.github.io/mds/algebra-exponentials.html#def-logarithm), $C$ is measured in [bits](entropy.qmd#def-bit) per channel use.

:::
